title: Togo protocol v1
description: Messages exchanged between the Togo app and the togo helper (`togo serve --stdio`). Transport: each message is a 4-byte big-endian unsigned length followed by that many bytes of UTF-8 JSON (one JSON-RPC 2.0 object, no batches). Max frame 1,048,576 bytes. `hello` must be the first call; every other call before a successful hello gets -32002 not_ready. Every response carries the id of the request it answers; clients must match responses to requests by id, not by order. Senders must follow the params schemas; the helper ignores unknown params fields.

Id.description: JSON-RPC request id. The app uses positive integers.

Request.description: A JSON-RPC 2.0 call. Methods with no required params may omit `params`.

Notification.description: A JSON-RPC 2.0 notification (no id). The helper ignores notifications it receives. It sends `event` only to a connection that called events.subscribe, and `harness` (harness.v1) only to a connection that called harness.open for that session.

Response.description: A JSON-RPC 2.0 response: exactly one of `result` or `error`. `id` echoes the request id, or is null when it could not be read (parse error).

Error.description: JSON-RPC error object. `message` is fixed per code: -32700 "parse error", -32600 "invalid request", -32601 "method not found", -32602 "invalid params" (with data {reason: human-readable detail, or for the methods that name one a fixed word: session.create args, program or not_installed; agents.check program; session.restore not_installed; session.sendText text; authkeys.remove key}), -32603 "internal error" (no details, never secrets), -32001 "not_found" (no such session), -32002 "not_ready" (call before a successful hello), -32003 "invalid_path" (fs.listDir: path not absolute after ~ expansion, contains NUL, missing, not a directory, or not readable; fs.read and git.*: path not relative, escaping the session cwd by .. or a symlink, missing, or a ref that starts with - or does not resolve; session.restore: the session's folder no longer exists), -32004 "tmux_unavailable" (data {found: version string or null when tmux is missing, required: "3.2"}), -32005 "unsupported_version" (hello with a protocol the helper does not speak; data {supported: [1]}), -32006 "conflict" (the target is not in a state that allows the call; data {reason, by?}. approval.answer: answered, prompt_gone or expired, with by "desk" | "phone" when reason is answered; git writes: a refusal with data GitConflictData, nothing changed except for reasons partial and raced; session.relaunch: running (the agent still runs); session.sendText: shell (the session is the plain shell, not an agent), ended (the agent exited, or a shell is back in the foreground of the agent's pane) or needs_you (an approval is pending); authkeys.remove: symlink, missing or not_regular (authorized_keys is a symlink, absent, or not a regular file); harness.send: busy (mode now while the agent works)), -32007 "not_managed" (write call on an unmanaged session, including git.stage, git.unstage, git.discard and git.commit), -32008 "refused" (the helper will not do this until the user sets it up on the machine; data {reason: "needs_admin_setup"}; or, for harness.*, the session has no adapter, data {reason: "no_adapter"}, or the screen or action cannot be served and the app should show the terminal, data {reason: "fallback", detail: "source" | "version" | "parse"}). `data` is omitted when a code defines none.

ManagedSessionId.description: Managed session id: `s_` + 10 chars of lowercase unpadded base32. Also the tmux session name on socket `togo`.

UnmanagedSessionId.description: Unmanaged session id: `u_` + lowercase hex of the tmux session name on the user's default socket.

SessionIdParam.description: Session id as sent in params. Any string is accepted on the wire; one matching neither ManagedSessionId nor UnmanagedSessionId gets -32602 invalid params with data.reason.

Timestamp.description: RFC 3339 timestamp. The helper emits UTC with a `Z` suffix and whole seconds.

Session.description: A tmux session. Managed sessions live on socket `togo`; unmanaged ones are read-only views of the user's default socket.

bib.description: Two-digit number 01-99, lowest free at creation. Null for unmanaged sessions.

name.description: Display name. Managed: Trimmed of leading and trailing Unicode whitespace, then 1-64 Unicode scalar values (Go runes, not bytes or grapheme clusters), with no control characters (Unicode Cc). Unmanaged: the tmux session name as is.

agent.description: Agent id from agents.list. Unmanaged sessions report `shell`.

cwd.description: Absolute working directory of the session's active pane.

status.description: `needs_you` while an approval for the session is pending, else the status the helper derived from hooks and output, else `exited` when the pane is dead and `idle` otherwise. Helpers without events.v1 report only `idle` and `exited`. With lifecycle.v1, a managed agent session whose agent process exits is `ended` (exit code 0, or interrupted) or `failed` (non-zero exit, an error or a usage limit), never `done`; both carry `exit`. A later agent hook for the session clears them.

activity.description: Short description of what the agent is doing, or null when unknown.

muted.description: Pushes for this session are suppressed (session.setMute). False by default; always false for unmanaged sessions.

meta.description: Agent-reported model and usage, all null until an agent hook reports them.

command.description: launch.v1: the argv the session's agent was started with, program then args, for managed agent sessions; null for shell and unmanaged sessions. Absent from helpers without launch.v1.

exit.description: lifecycle.v1: how the agent process ended while status is ended or failed, else null. Absent from helpers without lifecycle.v1.

activityHistory.description: Recent output volume of a managed session: at most 16 numbers in 0...1, oldest first, the last covering the current 30 second bucket. Each is the share of that bucket's seconds in which the session produced output. Optional: absent when the helper has seen no output yet or does not report it. Clients ignore it when absent.

mission.description: harness.v1: the harness summary for a session an adapter serves; absent otherwise. Clients ignore it when absent.

HelloParams.description: hello. The helper answers -32005 unsupported_version unless protocol is 1.

HelloResult.description: Base helper capabilities: ["session.v1", "agents.v1", "fs.v1", "capture.v1"]; capture.v1 adds session.capture. A helper adds, only when the running process serves them: "events.v1" (events.subscribe, events.keepalive and the event notification), "approvals.v1" (approval.list, approval.answer), "mute.v1" (session.setMute), "push.v1" (push.pair, push.unpair), "git.v1" (git.status, git.diff, git.log, git.branches, fs.read, fs.listDir with ref), "gitwrite.v1" (git.stage, git.unstage, git.discard, git.commit and git.diff with commit; only alongside git.v1), "ports.v1" (ports.list), "upload.v1" (fs.upload), "image.v1" (fs.image), "awake.v1" (awake.status, awake.set and the awake event), "launch.v1" (session.create program and args, agents.check, session.relaunch, Session.command), "lifecycle.v1" (Session statuses ended and failed with Session.exit, push kinds ended and failed, local.signal kind exit), "restore.v1" (session.restorable, session.restore, session.dismiss), "notify.v1" (notify.get, notify.set), "reply.v1" (session.sendText), "authkeys.v1" (authkeys.remove), "hostinfo.v1" (host.info), "browser.v1" (browser.openOnMac and the browser.open event), "harness.v1" (harness.describe, harness.open, harness.close, harness.history, harness.screen, harness.action, harness.send, harness.interrupt, harness.complete, harness.locate, the harness notification and Session.mission), "integrations.v1" (integrations.status, integrations.install, integrations.uninstall), "recent.v1" (fs.forgetRecentDir). local.* methods are never advertised.

SessionListResult.description: session.list. Managed sessions first ordered by bib, then unmanaged ordered by name.

SessionCreateParams.description: session.create -> Session. agent defaults to "shell"; cwd defaults to the home directory and may start with ~; name defaults to the agent's display name; cols 0 or 20-500 (0 = 80); rows 0 or 5-300 (0 = 24). Unknown or not installed agent, bad name, or out-of-range size: -32602. Bad cwd: -32003. All 99 bibs in use: -32602. cols and rows of 0 mean the defaults 80 and 24.

name.description: Trimmed of leading and trailing Unicode whitespace, then 1-64 Unicode scalar values (Go runes, not bytes or grapheme clusters), with no control characters (Unicode Cc), else -32602. Omitted, or empty after trimming, means the agent's display name.

program.description: launch.v1. Only with agent "custom", and then required; with any other agent -32602 reason program. Either a bare name matching ^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._+-]{0,63}$ found on the login-shell PATH, or an absolute path of at most 1024 bytes equal to its filepath.Clean form; either way it must name a regular executable file. Anything else is -32602 reason program; a well-formed name or path that is not found is -32602 reason not_installed. A managed agent that is not installed is also -32602 reason not_installed. name defaults to the program's base name.

args.description: launch.v1. Extra arguments for the agent's program, each delivered as one argv entry exactly as sent and never read by a shell or by tmux. 0-64 entries, each 1-4096 bytes of valid UTF-8 with no control characters (Unicode Cc, which includes NUL), at most 16,384 bytes in total; not allowed with agent "shell" (or with agent absent). Anything else is -32602 reason args.

muted.description: Optional: start the session muted, so nothing it asks or does reaches a push or the Live Activity, even before a later session.mute. Absent means false.

SessionExit.description: lifecycle.v1: how a session's agent process ended. code is the exit status, null when the process did not report one (killed by a signal, or a usage limit seen by a hook). reason: exit (the process exited; code says how), interrupted (stopped by Ctrl-C or a signal), error (the agent reported an error), usage_limit (the agent stopped on a usage limit). detail is a short plain-text explanation written by the helper, never raw terminal or agent text: it is cleaned exactly like a push body (ANSI sequences, control, bidirectional, zero-width, box drawing and block element characters removed, white space collapsed), cut to its first line and to 200 Unicode scalar values, and null when nothing is left. An ended session carries exit with code 0 or interrupted, or exit with code null when the helper found the agent already gone as it started; a failed one carries exit with a non-zero code, error or usage_limit.

AgentsCheckParams.description: agents.check (launch.v1) -> AgentsCheckResult. program follows the SessionCreateParams.program rules; a malformed one is -32602 reason program.

AgentsCheckResult.description: installed: program names a regular executable file, found on the login-shell PATH for a bare name. path is its absolute path, or null when installed is false.

SessionRelaunchParams.description: session.relaunch (launch.v1) -> Session. Runs the session's command again in its pane, keeping id, bib, name and cwd; exit becomes null. Bad id: -32602; unknown: -32001; u_ id: -32007; the agent still running: -32006 reason running.

RestorableSession.description: restore.v1: a managed session that a host restart ended, as the helper recorded it. command is as in Session. endedAt is when the helper last saw it. resumable: the agent can continue its previous conversation (session.restore with resume true).

SessionRestoreParams.description: session.restore (restore.v1) -> Session. Starts a restorable session again with its id, bib, name, cwd and command, and removes it from session.restorable. resume true continues the agent's previous conversation when the record is resumable. Unknown id: -32001; the folder no longer exists: -32003; the agent no longer installed: -32602 reason not_installed.

SessionSendTextParams.description: session.sendText (reply.v1) -> {}. Types text into the agent's pane literally; submit presses Enter after it. text: 1-8000 Unicode scalar values with no control characters (Unicode Cc) other than newline, else -32602 reason text. Bad id: -32602; unknown: -32001; u_ id: -32007. Refused with -32006 and nothing typed when the session is the plain shell, not an agent (reason shell), the agent has exited or a shell is back in the foreground of its pane (ended), or an approval is pending (needs_you).

IntegrationsChangeParams.description: integrations.install and integrations.uninstall (integrations.v1) -> IntegrationsChangeResult. agents: registry ids of harnesses that take hooks (claude, codex, gemini, auggie, droid, copilot), each at most once; anything else is -32602 (reason unknown_agent) and nothing changes. install with no agents sets up every harness installed on the machine; uninstall needs at least one. block also hooks the harness's approval event so the phone can answer (claude, codex, copilot). The helper runs its own installer as the user: it backs each file up once (<file>.togo-backup) before Togo's first change, writes nothing when nothing changes, chains Claude Code's own status line, refuses a Togo entry the user changed by hand, and uninstall restores each file byte for byte when nothing else changed since.

IntegrationReport.description: One harness's setup state. installed: the harness's program (and, for one that takes hooks, its config folder) is on the machine. setup: hooks (Togo writes hook entries), none (it talks to Togo another way: nothing to set up) or pending (it has hooks, not confirmed yet: nothing is written). state: ready, needsSetup, outdated (an older Togo's entries; install updates them), notNeeded, notSupported or notInstalled; clients show unknown values as needsSetup. hooks: installed, outdated or absent, for setup hooks. statusLine, for a harness whose status line Togo chains: chained (the user's own runs after Togo's and prints as before), togo (Togo's own; the user had none), own (the user's, not chained yet) or absent. path: the file Togo edits; backup: its copy from before Togo's first change, when there is one. lastHookAt and statusLineAt: when the helper last received the harness's hook and its status line (RFC 3339, UTC), absent when never. fix: the command that sets it up on the machine, when it needs one.

IntegrationsStatus.description: integrations.status (integrations.v1) -> this result: one row per harness the helper knows, in registry order (the rows `togo doctor` prints).

IntegrationOutcome.description: One harness's install or uninstall outcome. state: installed, unchanged, removed, skipped (not installed on the machine) or refused, with error saying why (the file could not be parsed, or a Togo entry was changed by hand); a refused harness's files are left as they were.

IntegrationsChangeResult.description: integrations.install and integrations.uninstall result: each harness's outcome, then every row after the change.

NotifySettings.description: notify.get and notify.set result (notify.v1): this machine's push settings. idleSeconds: quiet output after work before done is sent, 3-600, default 6. muted: this machine sends no pushes except clear, which takes away notifications already shown; default false. remindMinutes: one reminder for an approval still waiting after this many minutes, 0 (off) or 2-120, default 10.

NotifySetParams.description: notify.set (notify.v1) -> NotifySettings. At least one field; fields left out keep their value. A value outside the NotifySettings ranges is -32602 and nothing changes.

SSHPublicKey.description: An OpenSSH public key: type and base64 blob, no options and no comment.

AuthkeysRemoveParams.description: authkeys.remove (authkeys.v1) -> AuthkeysRemoveResult. Removes from ~/.ssh/authorized_keys the lines whose key blob equals publicKey and whose comment starts with togo@; every other byte and the file mode stay. A malformed key: -32602 reason key. authorized_keys a symlink, missing or not a regular file: -32006 reason symlink, missing or not_regular, and nothing is written.

AuthkeysRemoveResult.description: removed: lines removed, 0 when none matched.

HostInfo.description: host.info (hostinfo.v1): what a phone needs to wake and reach this machine. interfaces: up, non-loopback interfaces with a hardware address, each with its lowercase MAC and IPv4 addresses. wakeOnLan: the machine reports wake on LAN enabled, false when disabled, null when unknown. routes: see the property.

routes.description: Addresses a phone can try to reach this machine by, best for a local network first: kind mdns is the .local name, kind lan a private IPv4 or routable IPv6 address of interface, kind tailscale the MagicDNS name then the tailnet addresses (only while Tailscale is connected). Never link-local addresses. Older helpers omit it.

SessionKillParams.description: session.kill -> {}. An id matching neither the managed nor the unmanaged id pattern: -32602 with data.reason. Unknown managed id: -32001. Any `u_` id: -32007 not_managed, decided from the id alone; the user's tmux socket is never touched.

SessionRenameParams.description: session.rename -> Session. name: Trimmed of leading and trailing Unicode whitespace, then 1-64 Unicode scalar values (Go runes, not bytes or grapheme clusters), with no control characters (Unicode Cc); empty after trimming is -32602. An id matching neither id pattern: -32602 with data.reason. Unknown managed id: -32001. Any `u_` id: -32007.

SessionCaptureParams.description: session.capture -> SessionCaptureResult. Read-only; works for managed and unmanaged sessions. lines: history lines above the visible screen, 1-10000, default 1000; the visible rows are always included after them. With join true a wrapped line counts as several rows, so the result can hold fewer lines than `lines`. join: rejoin lines the terminal wrapped, default true. lines outside 1-10000, or an id matching neither id pattern: -32602. Unknown id: -32001.

SessionCaptureResult.description: text: plain text with no escape sequences and no trailing blank rows. When the JSON-encoded reply would not fit in one frame (1 MiB; escaping makes characters such as <, >, &, quotes and newlines take 2 to 6 bytes), the oldest lines are dropped, the newest are kept whole, and truncated is true. Text over 900000 bytes is cut the same way.

SessionAttachCommandParams.description: session.attachCommand. Works for managed and unmanaged sessions. An id matching neither id pattern: -32602 with data.reason. Unknown id: -32001.

SessionAttachCommandResult.description: argv to run on the host: [tmux path, "-u", socket args..., "attach-session", "-t", "=" + tmux session name]. The tmux path is absolute whenever the helper found tmux, so it runs under the minimal PATH of an SSH exec channel. Managed: [tmux, "-u", "-L", label, "attach-session", "-t", "=s_..."]. Unmanaged: [tmux, "-u", "attach-session", "-t", "=" + name]. A name ending in ";" has a backslash inserted before that ";", because tmux reads a trailing ";" as a command separator. An SSH exec request carries one command string that the host account's login shell parses, so clients executing argv over an SSH exec channel must POSIX single-quote every element, argv[0] included, and join the quoted elements with single spaces. The quoting rule: wrap the element in ' and replace each ' inside it with the four characters '\'' (close the quote, a backslash-escaped quote, reopen). For example it's becomes 'it'\''s'. The rule assumes a POSIX shell (sh, bash, zsh, dash, ksh).

installed.description: Command found on the user's login-shell PATH or in the common install folders. Always true for shell.

path.description: Absolute path of the command when installed. Absent for shell.

offPath.description: True when the command was found only in an install folder, not on the login-shell PATH; sessions then launch it by this path. Absent otherwise.

AgentsListResult.description: agents.list. Order in v1: claude (Claude Code), omp (OMP), codex (Codex), opencode (OpenCode), gemini (Gemini CLI), copilot (Copilot CLI), cursor (Cursor CLI), aider (Aider), amp (Amp), auggie (Auggie), cline (Cline), crush (Crush), droid (Droid), goose (Goose), kilo (Kilo Code), kimi (Kimi Code), kiro (Kiro CLI), openhands (OpenHands), pi (Pi), vibe (Mistral Vibe), shell (Shell). Clients show ids they do not know by name, so the list may grow within v1.

FsRecentDirsResult.description: fs.recentDirs. Absolute paths of folders used for session.create, newest first, deduplicated, at most 5. Temporary folders (under /tmp, /private/tmp, /var/folders or $TMPDIR outside home, or inside a folder named scratchpad) are never recorded, and folders that no longer exist are left out. When none are listed: [home directory].

FsForgetRecentDirParams.description: fs.forgetRecentDir (recent.v1) -> {}. Takes path off fs.recentDirs, compared as listed after a leading ~ is expanded to the home directory. A path that is not listed is no error.

FsListDirParams.description: fs.listDir. path must be absolute or start with ~ (expanded to the home directory); relative paths, NUL bytes, missing paths, non-directories and directories the user cannot read are -32003. showHidden (default false) includes names starting with a dot. includeFiles (default false) lists files and symlinks as well as directories; symlinks are never followed. With ref (git.v1), id is required and path is relative to the session cwd: the listing is the tree at that commit, with the same -32003 rules as fs.read. root (gitwrite.v1) needs id and makes path relative to the root of the repository holding the session cwd, as in fs.read; without ref it lists that folder on disk.

FsListDirResult.description: path is the cleaned absolute path that was listed. Without includeFiles, entries are subdirectories only (symlinks to directories included, at a ref only trees), with dir true and no kind or size. With includeFiles, entries are directories, regular files and symlinks, each with kind; dir is true only for kind dir; size (bytes) is given for files only; symlinks are reported as kind symlink and not followed; submodules, sockets, devices and pipes are left out. Sorted case-insensitively by name, at most 2000.

RequestId.description: Approval id: `r_` + 10 chars of lowercase unpadded base32.

HostId.description: Host id: `h_` + the first 26 chars of lowercase unpadded base32 of SHA-256(mailbox secret).

JobId.description: Job id: `j_` + 10 chars of lowercase unpadded base32.

Key32.description: A 32-byte key in base64url without padding (43 chars).

SessionMeta.description: What agent hooks and status-line payloads report about a session. Each field is null until reported.

ApprovalOption.description: One answer offered by the prompt. n is the number the agent's menu shows; option:<n> picks it.

Subject.description: The one thing an approval asks about, so notifications, the Live Activity and the Watch can show it without screen text. text counts Unicode scalar values and allows no control characters (Unicode Cc) other than newline and no bidirectional or zero-width characters (U+202A-202E, U+2066-2069, U+200B-200F, U+061C, U+2060, U+FEFF).

Approval.description: A question waiting for the user. Only pending approvals are listed or sent; the end of one is the approval.closed event.

source.description: hook: an agent permission hook; screen: the prompt-shape detector; ask: `togo ask`.

subject.description: Absent or null when the helper found no subject; detail then still describes the request. When set, detail is subject.text truncated to 256 characters, for apps that do not read subject.

snippet.description: Last lines of the pane around the prompt, at most 40 lines and 4096 bytes.

signIn.description: Optional: the prompt is a sign-in step read off the screen. url is the http or https page to open (at most 4096 bytes), code a device code to enter or confirm there (at most 16 characters), secret true when the agent waits for a pasted API key or authorization code; allowText is then true and a text answer is pasted into the pane as one bracketed paste followed by Enter, never typed key by key and never logged. Absent for every other prompt.

answerable.description: False while the helper cannot deliver an answer from the phone (a hook request with no options and no screen fingerprint yet); the app then shows it as waiting in the terminal. Absent means true.

Decision.description: approve | deny | option:<n> (1-99, no leading zero) | text:<1-2000 Unicode scalar values (not UTF-16 units), no control characters (Unicode Cc)>. approve picks the first option with role approve (never approve_always); deny picks the first with role deny, else sends Escape. option:<n> naming no offered option and text: when allowText is false are -32602. Answers arriving through the relay mailbox may only be approve, deny or option:<n>.

Event.description: params of the `event` notification. The kind-specific fields sit beside the header fields. seq is strictly increasing per daemon and starts at 1. Every subscriber receives every event (no per-connection filtering), so a seq gap always means lost events and the client must call events.subscribe again. The helper writes the events.subscribe response before any event for that subscription; a client drops every event with seq <= the response seq. sessionId equals session.id for kind session, is non-null for session.removed and approval.open/closed of a session, and is null for events that belong to no session (notify and job without a session, and awake, which a helper with awake.v1 sends whenever its awake status changes). browser.open (browser.v1) says an agent asked to open a web page: url is an http or https URL the helper validated; sessionId names the managed session whose agent asked, or is null. It is sent only while an app is subscribed in the foreground; with none, the helper opens the page on the machine instead.

SessionRefParams.description: Params naming one session: git.status, git.branches, ports.list, session.dismiss. Bad id: -32602; unknown: -32001. session.dismiss (restore.v1) -> {} deletes a restorable session's record without running anything.

EventsSubscribeParams.description: events.subscribe. Starts event notifications on this connection and returns a snapshot. foreground (default true) says the app is on screen, which suppresses pushes for sessions the app shows; call again to change it. Foreground is a lease: it lapses 45 s after the last request the connection sent, and any request renews it. An idle app on screen calls events.keepalive about every 20 s.

EventsKeepaliveParams.description: events.keepalive. Does nothing but, like every request, renews the connection's foreground lease (see EventsSubscribeParams). Result is {}.

EventsSubscribeResult.description: events.subscribe result. seq is the seq of the last event already reflected in sessions and approvals (0 when none). This response is written before any event for the subscription; events with seq <= this seq are already in the snapshot and the client drops them. Calling events.subscribe again on the same connection returns a fresh snapshot under the same rule and does not duplicate the stream.

ApprovalListParams.description: approval.list. Pending approvals, oldest first, optionally for one session.

ApprovalAnswerParams.description: approval.answer. Unknown requestId: -32001. Malformed decision (see Decision) or option n not offered: -32602. Already answered, prompt gone or expired: -32006, and no keys reach the pane.

SessionSetMuteParams.description: session.setMute -> Session. Bad id or muted missing: -32602; unknown: -32001; u_ id: -32007.

PushPairParams.description: push.pair. x25519: the device's push-sealing public key; approvalKey: its Ed25519 answer-signing public key. Pairing an existing deviceId replaces it. Any field out of shape: -32602. platform is ios when absent. liveActivityStartToken is the push-to-start token for the Live Activity; liveActivityCommand (default false) lets Live Activity pushes carry command text.

sshKey.description: The public key this device uses to sign in over SSH, so authkeys.remove can take it off the machine when the device forgets it. Send it only when the helper advertises authkeys.v1: an older helper rejects push.pair with a field it does not know.

PushPairResult.description: hostKey is the helper's X25519 public key, which seals answers sent through the relay mailbox.

GitStatusResult.description: git.status. A cwd outside any repository is repo false, root and branch null, zero counts and no files. branch is null on a detached HEAD. The helper runs git with repository config that executes programs disabled. A helper with gitwrite.v1 lists every untracked file on its own (never a folder entry, as git status --untracked-files=all), lists at most 2,000 files in git's order, and always sends truncated, true when it left files out. Absent truncated (an older helper) means false. A client must not offer an action on all changes (such as discarding everything) while truncated is true.

items.description: index and worktree are the porcelain v2 status letters, `.` when unchanged. fingerprint (gitwrite.v1) identifies the working-tree content; every untracked or changed file present in the working tree has one, and it is absent only when the path has no file there (deleted).

GitDiffParams.description: git.diff. path is relative to the repository root, like git.status paths, and the diff runs at the root, so a session in a subfolder of the repository diffs any path git.status lists. ref diffs the working tree (or the index with staged) against that commit. commit (gitwrite.v1) diffs that commit against its first parent, a root commit against the empty tree; commit with staged true or with ref is -32602. Path, ref or commit rules as fs.read: -32003.

GitDiffResult.description: diff is unified text capped at 512 KiB; binary lists paths whose content differs but is not shown.

GitLogParams.description: git.log. ref defaults to HEAD, limit to 50. A ref starting with - or not resolving: -32003.

GitBranchesResult.description: git.branches. Local branches by name. Outside a repository: current null, no branches.

GitPathsParams.description: git.stage, git.unstage, git.discard (gitwrite.v1). Paths are relative to the repository root, like git.status paths. Each path names one file (GitWritePath) and follows the fs.read rules (-32003); a path of more than 4,096 bytes, with a NUL, ending in / or naming a directory is -32602, so a write never acts on a whole folder. The helper reads a fresh status first and refuses the whole call with -32006 stale when a path is not in it with a change the method acts on (stage: worktree change, untracked or unmerged; unstage: index change; discard: any change), or when seen has the path and either its status differs from the fresh letters or its fingerprint differs from a freshly computed one (one present and the other absent also differs). A file edited again keeps its letters but changes its fingerprint. Paths with a filter attribute (such as Git LFS) are -32006 filtered, a held index.lock is -32006 locked, and git.discard of an unmerged path is -32006 unmerged; in each case nothing is changed. git.discard acts on each path by itself: a path in HEAD has its index entry and working-tree file restored to HEAD (staged and unstaged changes both go); a path not in HEAD (untracked, or added in the index only) is removed from the index if there and its file is deleted. A path staged as a rename (index R) undoes the rename: its origPath is restored to HEAD in the index and working tree in the same write, and the new path is removed; the call is -32006 stale when anything is on disk at origPath under any letter case (a listed, ignored or untracked file, a link or a folder), or when seen has the new path but not origPath with the same status and no fingerprint, and -32006 case_rename when origPath differs from the path only in letter case. The partial changed list includes origPath when it changed. Nothing else changes: no other path, no ignored file and no folder. git.unstage of a path staged as a rename also puts its origPath back in the index. The result is the status after the write. Paths are passed to git literally, after --, and no hook, filter or other repository-configured program runs.

seen.description: Optional for git.stage and git.unstage; git.discard needs an entry for every path (-32602 otherwise). For each path, what git.status reported when the user chose it: status is the index and worktree letters, index first (".M" is a worktree change, "??" an untracked file), and fingerprint is the entry's fingerprint, absent when the entry had none. For a staged rename the client also sends its origPath with the rename's status and no fingerprint, so git.discard restores only the old path the user saw.

GitWritePath.description: One file path for a git write: 1 to 4,096 UTF-8 bytes (the schema can only bound characters) with no NUL. A path ending in / is also -32602; that rule is pinned by a fixture rather than this schema.

GitFingerprint.description: Content id of a working-tree file, compared only for equality. blob:<hash> is git's blob hash of the file bytes as stored without filters (git hash-object --no-filters), used for regular files up to 8,388,608 bytes while the blob-hashed files so far in the status list (git's order) total at most 268,435,456 bytes. stat:<size>:<mtime_ns> is the lstat size in bytes and modification time in nanoseconds since the epoch, used for larger files, for symlinks, and for every regular file from the first one that would pass that total.

GitCommitParams.description: git.commit (gitwrite.v1). Commits the index with message, or replaces the HEAD commit with amend. message is 1 to 65,536 UTF-8 bytes, its first line is not empty after trimming, and it has no control characters other than \n and \t; otherwise -32602. amend without head is -32602. Nothing staged without amend is -32006 nothing_staged, amend with no commit yet is -32006 unborn_amend, a missing git user.name or user.email is -32006 identity, a held index.lock is -32006 locked, and head that is no longer HEAD is -32006 stale. Hooks and commit signing never run.

head.description: The HEAD commit hash the user saw: required with amend (the commit it replaces), optional otherwise.

GitConflictData.description: -32006 data for a git write. stale: a path or HEAD no longer matches what the client saw. locked: another git process holds the index lock. filtered: a path has a filter attribute. unmerged: a conflicted path that the method does not act on. nothing_staged, identity, unborn_amend: see GitCommitParams. case_rename: git.discard of a rename that only changes letter case, which the helper does not undo. For all of these nothing changed. partial: the write failed after changing some paths; changed lists the paths whose status differs from before the call, and the client should refresh. raced: git.commit made commit hash, but another process moved HEAD between the helper's check and the commit, so its parent is not the HEAD the user saw; nothing is rewritten.

FsReadParams.description: fs.read. path is relative to the session cwd; absolute paths, .. escapes, symlinks resolving outside the cwd, missing files and non-files are -32003. ref reads the file at that commit (a ref starting with - is -32003). root (gitwrite.v1) makes path relative to the root of the repository holding the session cwd instead, the form git.status paths take; the same -32003 rules apply against the root, and a session outside a repository is -32003.

FsReadResult.description: path echoes the cleaned relative path. size is the full file size in bytes; content holds at most 512 KiB, base64url without padding (the protocol-wide rule) when the bytes are not valid UTF-8.

FsUploadParams.description: fs.upload (upload.v1). Writes the bytes for the agent to read, such as a screenshot. sessionId must be a managed session id (an unmanaged one is -32007, an unknown one -32001; any other string is -32602). name is reduced to the characters A-Z a-z 0-9 . _ - and at most 64 bytes, keeping the extension; directory parts and leading dots are dropped. data is base64url without padding; more than 700000 decoded bytes is -32602.

FsUploadResult.description: path is the absolute path on the host of the file written, mode 0600 under $TOGO_HOME/uploads/<sessionId>/ as <unix-ms>-<name>. The helper deletes uploads older than 7 days.

FsImageParams.description: fs.image (image.v1). Reads a picture the chat shows. path must be absolute and clean with an image extension, and after symlinks inside $TOGO_HOME/uploads/<sessionId>/ or the session's working folder; anything else, or a file whose bytes are not PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP or HEIC, is -32602. sessionId must be a managed session id.

FsImageResult.description: data is the picture as base64url without padding, at most 700000 bytes. A larger PNG, JPEG or GIF is shrunk to a JPEG that fits (scaled true); any other larger picture, or one over 40 MiB, is -32602. bytes is the file's size on disk.

AwakeStatus.description: awake.status and awake.set result, and the awake event payload (awake.v1): whether the helper is keeping the machine awake. mode: off never holds; plugged (default) holds a sleep assertion while any managed session is working or needs_you and for 2 minutes after, which keeps a closed laptop awake on AC power only; battery also disables sleep so a closed lid stays awake on battery. held: a sleep block is in place now. reason: unsupported (platformSupported false), off, idle (no session working or waiting), active, grace (held for 2 minutes after the last active session), on_battery (plugged mode held on battery: a closed lid still sleeps), needs_admin_setup (battery mode before its one-time setup on the machine; behaves like plugged), battery_floor (battery mode paused at or below batteryFloor until 5 points above it or charging), thermal (battery mode paused by a thermal warning on battery), failed (detail says why). power and batteryPercent describe the power source; batteryPercent is absent without a battery or when unknown. needsAdmin: battery mode needs `togo awake battery` run on the machine first.

AwakeSetParams.description: awake.set -> AwakeStatus. At least one field. Changing mode to battery before the one-time setup on the machine is -32008 refused with data.reason needs_admin_setup; off and plugged are always allowed. An unknown mode or a batteryFloor outside 10-50 is -32602.

PortsListResult.description: ports.list. TCP ports in the LISTEN state held by processes in the session's process tree, ordered by port.

LocalSignalParams.description: local.signal -> {}. Sent by `togo tap` for a bell, an OSC 9 or OSC 777 notification, the first output after quiet, or a shell command mark (kind osc133: title is the mark, C or D, body the mark as JSON, code the command's exit status when the shell reported one), and by the launch wrapper with kind exit and the agent's exit status in code (0-255, required for exit and allowed only with it). local.* methods are served only by the daemon, on connections it accepts on its unix socket from the same user; `serve --stdio` proxies to that socket, so its connections get them too. The in-process server that `serve --stdio` falls back to without a daemon does not serve them.

LocalHookParams.description: local.hook -> {}. One agent hook invocation, reduced by the adapter. hook (the agent's own event name, or statusline) and payload (the agent's hook payload, redacted in the hook process, at most 256 KiB) are optional and only feed the session's harness adapter; event harness reaches the adapter alone and changes no status. Helpers that predate them send neither.

LocalQuestionParams.description: local.question -> {answers?: {<prompt>: <answer>}, reason: answered|timeout}. Sent by a blocking Claude Code AskUserQuestion hook: it holds the question dialog until the question item is answered from the phone, then replies with the answers keyed by question prompt (labels of a multi-select joined with ", "). Returns timeout at once when no device can answer.

LocalAskParams.description: local.ask. Opens an approval with source ask and blocks until it is answered or timeoutSec passes.

approve.description: The option a notification's Approve picks, matched case-insensitively. Absent: inferred from the labels (Approve, Yes, Allow, Accept, Continue).

deny.description: The option a notification's Deny picks, matched case-insensitively. Absent: inferred from the labels (Deny, No, Reject, Cancel, Stop).

WebUrl.description: An absolute http or https URL with a host, at most 4096 bytes of printable ASCII (no spaces). The helper rejects anything else with -32602.

BrowserOpenOnMacParams.description: browser.openOnMac (browser.v1) -> {}. Opens url in the machine's default browser, as the user asked from the phone. The app sends only a WebUrl; the helper checks it again and answers anything else, such as a file URL, with -32602 and opens nothing.

LocalOpenUrlParams.description: local.openUrl, sent by `togo open-url`, which the open, xdg-open and BROWSER shims of a managed session run. The helper publishes a browser.open event when an app is subscribed in the foreground, waiting a few seconds for one to attach.

LocalOpenUrlResult.description: local.openUrl result. delivered false means no app took the page, so the caller opens it on the machine.

LocalNotifyParams.description: local.notify. strict makes `togo notify` exit non-zero when nothing was delivered.

LocalNotifyResult.description: delivered is true when a subscriber or a paired device received it.

LocalJobParams.description: local.job. start needs name and returns a new jobId; update and end need jobId; end takes status (default ok).

LocalShutdownParams.description: local.shutdown -> LocalShutdownResult. Sent by `togo serve` when the daemon reports a different version than the installed binary, and by `togo daemon restart` and `togo update`. when idle: the daemon exits with status 75 once no approval is open and no local.ask call is waiting, which may be at once; its service manager or the next serve starts the installed binary. Repeated requests are answered with the current count and change nothing. reason is recorded in the daemon log.

LocalShutdownResult.description: deferred is true while pending approvals and asks hold the exit back.

HarnessAnchor.description: Where in the pane's output an item happened, for Show in terminal.

epoch.description: Names the pane's output stream; changes when the pane respawns or the tap restarts.

bytes.description: Output bytes the tap had seen in this epoch when the item arrived.

line.description: Absolute grid line of the cursor when the item arrived: history lines plus the cursor row.

needle.description: Up to 120 runes of text near the line, to confirm or search.

HarnessImage.description: A picture in the conversation: inline (base64url, at most 48 KiB decoded) when small, else by absolute path for fs.image, or only described.

output.description: Tail of the tool's output, at most 4096 bytes, secrets removed.

owner.description: The id of the question item that is the same prompt. The question item answers it; clients do not draw this approval on its own.

answerable.description: False when the harness offers no way to answer from the phone; the app shows the questions read-only with Answer in the terminal. Absent means true.

requestId.description: The pending approval that is this question at the terminal, when one is linked (its approval item carries owner = this item's id).

output.description: Tail of what the command printed, plain text, at most 4 KiB. Set once the block finished.

HarnessItem.description: One conversation entry (harness.v1). id is stable: an update resends the item with the same id and a new seq, and the client replaces it. The body sits under the key named by kind; other body keys are absent. parent is the agent item whose own conversation holds this item.

HarnessRow.description: A line in a mission control section or a live list.

HarnessStatus.description: The Status primitive and the mission control status section.

MissionSummary.description: Session.mission (harness.v1): the activity pill and roster line.

HarnessMission.description: Mission control snapshot. sections holds only the sections the harness supports, in the fixed order needs, agents, background, plan, changes, ports, status.

HarnessDelta.description: Moves a mission from rev-1 to rev. A client holding any other rev calls harness.open again.

onSelectLabel.description: onSelect's own words for an item's button (omp: Use for this session).

setup.description: What is not set up yet (a provider not signed in), shown after the items.

setupAction.description: Sets up one setup entry, run with args {id} (and {value} when setupInput is set).

setupInput.description: secret: the setup action asks for a value first, such as an API key.

value.description: The current value; always null for secret fields, whose isSet says whether one exists.

HarnessScreen.description: harness.screen result: one of the seven primitives, filled by the adapter. Exactly the key named by primitive is set. stale is true when the source failed and this is the last good copy.

HarnessDescribeResult.description: harness.describe result. adapter is null when no adapter serves the session; the app then shows the terminal only.

capabilities.description: Session capabilities: chat, chat.stream, chat.history, chat.anchors, send.api, send.queue, interrupt, commands, files, mode, model, effort, needs.approvals, needs.questions, agents, background, plan, changes, ports, status, status.usage, status.context, resume, compact, mcp, settings. Clients ignore unknown values.

degraded.description: Capabilities the adapter declares whose sources failed or whose version gate refused this harness version.

images.description: How the harness takes image paths in a prompt. per_path pastes each path on its own, then the text; together pastes them at once. Absent: together.

HarnessOpenParams.description: harness.open. after is the client's cursor (0 for none); limit caps the items returned, newest kept (default 200).

HarnessOpenResult.description: harness.open result. The response is written before any harness notification for the session on this connection; the client drops notified items with seq <= cursor. more is true when older items exist (harness.history). A different epoch than the client held means its items are void.

HarnessActionParams.description: harness.action. target names the item or row acted on. Built-in actions: answer (args.answers maps question id to option ids or text), set_mode (args.id), interrupt, stop (target).

HarnessActionResult.description: applied: the harness confirmed it. typed: a documented command was typed and not yet confirmed. fallback: no route works; open the terminal.

HarnessSendParams.description: harness.send. queue (default) types now when the agent is idle, else holds the prompt until the turn ends; now is refused with -32006 reason busy while it works.

text.description: Same rules as session.sendText text; may be empty only when images are given.

images.description: Absolute, clean image paths (png, jpg, jpeg, gif, webp, heic) sent in the same prompt, usually files fs.upload wrote. Typed into the input as the adapter's images.insert says, then the text, then Enter once; through a harness API all go in the one request.

kind.description: How the palette runs the command. choice: a menu in place from choices; picker: push screen; args: to the composer, Return waits for the argument; run: runs at once; terminal: typed, and the app shows the terminal. Absent from older helpers: the app derives it from screen and hint.

role.description: destructive: the app asks in a system confirmation before running.

action.description: A harness.action id the command runs instead of typing its text (e.g. compact, undo).

opens.description: A native home the command opens instead of typing: status, changes, or a screen id.

choices.description: For kind choice: the values, with the current one selected.

HarnessSelectConfirm.description: Asked before a selection or field change runs. effect relaunch: the change restarts the agent; the app confirms only while it works and offers Undo when idle.

HarnessNotification.description: params of the `harness` notification (harness.v1), sent only to a connection that called harness.open for the session, until harness.close or the connection ends. items: new or updated items, seq increasing. mission: one delta. reset: the client must call harness.open again (adapter changed, epoch changed, or the connection fell behind).

PushPlaintext.description: Plaintext sealed (label push, aad hostId + "|" + deviceId) into the ciphertext of a relay push, encoded as compact UTF-8 JSON. kind needs_you announces an approval: requestId and options are required. kind clear withdraws the notification for requestId (required; the approval closed): title and body are empty strings and options is absent. done, job and notify carry no requestId or options. sessionId, bib and agent are null when the event belongs to no session. ts is Unix time in milliseconds when the helper sealed it. The push is not signed by the host; a forged push can only change what the phone displays, since answers are bound to the host's requestIds. subject (needs_you only, absent when unknown) is the approval's structured subject; host is the machine's display name (`hostname -s`, at most 64 characters). Both are optional so older payloads stay valid. lifecycle.v1 adds kind ended and failed (an agent process exited; exit, optional, is the SessionExit) and kind offline (the machine went quiet while sessions worked: sealed ahead of time and sent by the relay only when the helper's connection goes quiet; sessionId, bib and agent are null; active, optional, is how many sessions were working). These carry no requestId or options. reminder, optional and only on needs_you, is true on the one reminder for an approval still waiting. allowText, optional and only on needs_you, is true when the approval takes a typed answer (the phone offers Reply); the answer itself still travels only over SSH.

allowText.description: Optional, needs_you only: true when the approval takes a typed answer as well as its options. Absent means false.

sessionName.description: Optional: the session's name, the title of its notifications.

AnswerPlaintext.description:
Plaintext sealed (label answer, aad hostId) by the phone and posted to the relay mailbox, encoded as compact UTF-8 JSON. decision is limited to approve, deny and option:<n>; text answers travel only over SSH. ts is Unix time in milliseconds on the phone. sig is the Ed25519 signature, base64url without padding (86 chars), by the device's approvalKey over the UTF-8 bytes of "togo-approval/v1
" + hostId + "
" + requestId + "
" + decision + "
" + ts, where ts is written in decimal ASCII without leading zeros, each field is exactly the value in this object (hostId from push.pair), and there is no trailing newline. Senders omit type on answers, because helpers that predate it reject unknown fields; receivers accept it absent or "answer". Only RegisterPlaintext, which shares the mailbox, carries a type.

RegisterPlaintext.description:
Plaintext sealed (label answer, aad hostId) by a paired device and posted to the relay mailbox when its tokens or its command text choice change, encoded as compact UTF-8 JSON. A token left out keeps the stored one. liveActivityCommand replaces the stored choice (see PairParams). ts is Unix time in milliseconds on the device. sig is the Ed25519 signature, base64url without padding (86 chars), by the device's approvalKey over the UTF-8 bytes of "togo-register/v2
" + hostId + "
" + deviceId + "
" + apnsToken + "
" + liveActivityToken + "
" + liveActivityStartToken + "
" + liveActivityCommand + "
" + ts, where an absent token is the empty string, liveActivityCommand is "true" or "false", ts is decimal ASCII without leading zeros, and there is no trailing newline.

LiveContentState.description: Live Activity content state, sent by the helper to the relay in the clear and shown by the app. since is Unix time in seconds when the status began. requestId is the approval the Approve button answers, null unless status is needs_you. command is null unless the device opted in with liveActivityCommand.

reason.description: Present only when status is ended or failed: the exit reason word of the session. Never carries exit detail.

LiveAttributes.description: Live Activity attributes sent with a push-to-start.

PlaintextFixture.description: A sealed-payload example in protocol/v1/fixtures/plaintext. Shape only: protocol/fixtures/crypto holds the seal and signature vectors.

Fixture.description: Golden exchange in protocol/v1/fixtures. A harness starts a fresh connection, sends each `setup` request in order (each reply must be a success response; its result is not compared), then sends `request` and compares the reply to `response` semantically: same keys and values, with two placeholder rules for strings in `response`. (1) The string "<any>" matches any value (the key must still be present); it is used only for genuinely host-dependent values (tmux path and socket label in argv, os, arch, the -32602 reason text, git.commit hashes, which depend on the host clock; so the git.commit result is checked for shape only, not against GitCommitResult). (2) A string starting with "<home>" is replaced by the harness HOME path followed by the rest of the string ("<home>/proj" means HOME + "/proj"; "<home>" alone means HOME) and then compared exactly. Harness environment shared by all fixtures: a fresh, empty tmux server on a test label; no unmanaged sessions (user socket disabled); session ids come from a seam returning "s_abcdefghij"; the clock reads 2026-11-03T12:00:00Z; helper version "0.0.0-test", hostname "testhost"; HOME (and the API's home) is a fresh temp dir, given as an absolute path with symlinks resolved (so tmux's pane path equals it), holding directories `alpha`, `Beta`, `proj`, `.cache` and a regular file `notes.txt` (byte order Beta, alpha, proj differs from the case-insensitive order alpha, Beta, proj); TOGO_HOME is a separate fresh temp dir; the login-shell PATH contains none of claude, omp, codex, opencode. Per-fixture deviations are stated in `description`.
